contract: Shared pane-layout operation conformance cases. The Swift PaneLayoutState and the TUI's panes module both run every case; the fixture is the normative contract for the recursive split-tree model.

A layout is the durable projection: { version, groups: [{ id, representativePaneID, root }] }. A node is { pane: { id, sessionID } } or { split: { direction: horizontal|vertical, ratio, left, right } }.

Coordinates: (0,0) is top-left, x grows right, y grows down. A horizontal split lays left|right; a vertical split lays top/bottom with the LEFT child on top. Ratio is the left/top child's share, clamped to [0.1, 0.9] at construction, resize, migration, and restore.

version 1 initials use the flat shape { id, representativePaneID, panes: [{ id, sessionID, fraction }] } and exercise the read migration: panes fold right-leaning, node(i) = split(horizontal, clamp(f_i / (f_i + ... + f_n)), leaf(p_i), node(i+1)). Divide, then clamp. Readers must also accept the legacy Rust key spellings representativePaneId / sessionId for version 1 only.
Leaf order is preorder (left-first) traversal. It drives representative promotion, cap trimming, and expectLiveLeaves ordering. The session-leaf cap is 8; canonicalize trims trailing preorder leaves.

Insert splits the target leaf at ratio 0.5; the new leaf becomes the left child for edges left/up and the right child for edges right/down. Group-edge insert splits the root; the new leaf's share is 1/(sessionLeafCount+1), clamped.
Detach removes a leaf and collapses its parent split to the surviving sibling. A group dissolves below 2 session leaves unless exactly 1 session plus a live launcher remains.

Equalize sets each split's ratio to leftWeight/(leftWeight+rightWeight), where a child's weight is: leaf = 1, same-direction split = sum of its children's weights, perpendicular split = 1. Recurses into all splits.
swapPanes exchanges the positions of two leaves in the same group's tree; pane ids travel with their leaves, so the representative id is unaffected.

insertLauncher snapshots the group's pre-insert tree. removeLauncher restores the snapshot iff its session-leaf id set equals the launcher-stripped tree's. bindLauncher and any explicit geometry mutation (insert, resize, swap, equalize) clear the snapshot. Reconcile prunes the snapshot with the same removal algorithm and drops it below 2 leaves or on divergence.

The durable projection strips launcher leaves via the removal algorithm; while a launcher is live and a snapshot exists, the snapshot is what gets encoded. Groups with fewer than 2 session leaves are omitted. Durable writes are always version 2.

focusNeighbor is a pure query over the spatial subdivision of the group's tree using artificial grid dimensions (leaf = 1x1; horizontal split sums widths/maxes heights; vertical split sums heights/maxes widths). Candidate leaves must satisfy the edge predicate (left: candidate.maxX <= ref.minX; right: candidate.minX >= ref.maxX; up: candidate.maxY <= ref.minY; down: candidate.minY >= ref.maxY), sorted stably by Euclidean distance between top-left corners; preorder breaks ties. No candidate means null.

Harnesses decode 'initial' through the real durable codec (so canonicalize and migration run), apply 'operations' in order, then re-encode and compare structurally with ratio tolerance 1e-9. Never compare JSON strings. When 'error' is expected, all operations before the last must succeed and the last must fail with that error; the state comparison is skipped. 'expectLiveLeaves' asserts the live (pre-projection) leaves in preorder.
Pane and group ids must be canonical lowercase UUIDs (non-UUID ids are replaced at restore, which would break determinism). Session ids are opaque strings.
Zoom is process-local presentation state and deliberately absent from this contract.

cases.description: v1 flat pair folds into one horizontal split with ratio = first fraction.
v1 triple folds right-leaning: ratios 0.5 then 0.3/0.5.
Even quarters fold to ratios 0.25, 1/3, 0.5.
A fraction below the floor clamps the derived ratio to 0.1.
Migration keeps a non-first representative pane id.
A malformed v1 group with one pane cannot survive restore.
A session may appear once per layout; the later occurrence's leaf is dropped and its group dissolves below 2 leaves.
Out-of-range ratios in stored trees clamp to [0.1, 0.9] on restore.
A 9-leaf group trims trailing preorder leaves down to the 8-leaf cap, collapsing as it goes.
Splitting a leaf on its right edge wraps it in a horizontal split with the new leaf on the right.
Edge left places the new leaf as the left child.
Edge down creates a vertical split with the target on top.
Edge up creates a vertical split with the new leaf on top.
A group-edge insert splits the root; the new leaf's share is 1/(leafCount+1).
Inserting beside a solo session creates a fresh 0.5/0.5 group.
A session already in the layout cannot be inserted again.
An 8-leaf group refuses a ninth session.
Removing a leaf collapses its parent split to the surviving sibling.
Detaching the representative promotes the first remaining session leaf in preorder.
Detaching from a two-leaf group dissolves it.
Detaching a pane id absent from every group fails.
Closing a group removes it entirely.
An empty path addresses the root split.
A nested split addressed by path clamps its ratio to 0.9.
A path landing on a leaf is not a split.
A right-leaning chain of three equalizes to 1/3 then 1/2.
A perpendicular child counts as weight 1, so the outer split equalizes to 0.5.
Same-direction children sum their weights: 2 vs 2 leaves gives 0.5 at the root.
Swapping exchanges leaf positions anywhere in the tree; the representative id follows its pane.
Panes in different groups cannot swap.
An ineligible session's leaf is removed and the tree collapses around it.
Losing the representative promotes the first surviving session leaf in preorder.
A group left with one session and no launcher dissolves.
One session plus a live launcher survives reconcile; the pruned snapshot is dropped and the durable projection omits the under-2 group.
A fully eligible layout is untouched.
Canceling a launcher restores the exact pre-insert tree.
An explicit resize while the launcher is open clears the snapshot; cancel keeps the resized geometry.
Binding a launcher swaps its content in place; the pane id and geometry survive.
While a launcher is open the durable projection encodes the pre-launcher snapshot, not the live tree.
In a 2x2 grid, right of the top-left pane is the top-right pane.
Down from the top-left pane is the bottom-left pane (nearest by top-left distance).
Up from the bottom-right pane prefers the top-right pane over the farther top-left.
There is nothing left of the top-left pane.
From the bottom-right leaf of a mixed tree, left crosses to the tall left pane; the top-right pane does not qualify.
